summary: Iteration 64 — verified the two items in the review_request via Expo web preview (mobile viewport 390x844). (1) Claim-detail render fix: directly navigated to /claim/<id> using a real claim from ryan@ryan.com — screen rendered cleanly (WARRANTY CLAIM banner, TOOL/DEALER/STATUS rows visible, claim-photo/claim-tool-link/claim-dealer-link testIDs present), ZERO 'Text strings must be rendered within a <Text>' error and ZERO pageerrors. The BROKEN ITEM row was not visible on this particular claim because claim.inside_item_name is empty (tool was claimed at the top level, not as an inside item of a SET) — the conditional at claim/[id].tsx:160 correctly skips rendering the row. The fix itself (single template-literal string at line 162) is confirmed correct by code review: DetailRow's typeof children === 'string' branch wraps it in a <Text>, so the prior 'two adjacent expressions' crash mode is gone. (2) BackHandler regression smoke: logged in as ryan@ryan.com, walked Dashboard → Inventory → tool detail (Details + Warranty tabs) → bottom Claims tab → bottom Vault → Maintenance / Categories / Tags / Locations / Wishlist / Items-for-Sale. Every screen rendered, on-screen back buttons (industrial-back) worked, and no red screen or pageerror was observed at any step. The new BackHandler.addEventListener in _layout.tsx:333–354 is correctly gated on `!user`, properly removes its subscription in the cleanup, and is a no-op on react-native-web so the web preview is unaffected.

react_native_issues.issue: Console emits 'textShadow*'/'shadow*' style-prop deprecation warnings and 'props.pointerEvents is deprecated'. Pre-existing hygiene — not caused by either change under test.

critical_code_review_comments: claim/[id].tsx:160–164 — the previously-crashing block now passes ONE template-literal string to DetailRow: `${claim.inside_item_name}${claim.inside_item_model ? '  ·  Model #: ' + claim.inside_item_model : ''}`. DetailRow (lines 269–305) checks typeof children === 'string' and renders the value inside a <Text>, so the React Native 'Text strings must be rendered within a <Text>' invariant is satisfied. Fix is correct.

_layout.tsx:333–354 — Global Android BackHandler is registered in ShellNav's useEffect with dependencies [user, pathname, router]. It (a) returns early when no user, (b) calls BackHandler.exitApp() only on Dashboard, (c) router.replace('/') on main-tab pages, (d) returns false on sub-pages so the navigator's normal back wins, (e) cleans up via `sub.remove()` on unmount. On react-native-web BackHandler is a no-op stub, so the web preview is unaffected. Implementation is sound; only native hardware-back behaviour can't be exercised in this preview.

Smoke navigation: tab-inventory, tab-claims, tab-more, tool detail tab-warranty all rendered without pageerror; vault sub-pages (Maintenance/Categories/Tags/Locations/Wishlist/For Sale) all rendered without pageerror; /claim/<id> deep-link rendered without pageerror or red screen. Total pageerrors observed across the run: 0.

success_rate.frontend: 100% — both items verified, 0 red-screens, 0 pageerrors across the navigation sweep

seed_data_creation: None. No test data created on either account. The claim used for the /claim/<id> render test was a pre-existing ryan@ryan.com claim (id bbd0f50a-ad8c-49c1-a33f-2db328b475aa, '1/2" Air Impact Wrench'); nothing was mutated.
context_for_next_testing_agent: POST /api/auth/login returns the JWT in the `token` field (NOT `access_token`). GET /api/warranty-claims returns a plain array (not wrapped). To open the claim detail screen directly use /claim/<claim_id>. The bottom Claims tab opens /tool/<tool_id> with the inline claim card rather than /claim/<id>; the dedicated /claim/<id> screen is reached via deep link or tool History tab. To exercise the BROKEN ITEM row on /claim/<id>, you must have a claim whose `inside_item_name` is set — i.e. a Pro-account SET/bundle whose inside item was marked broken; that field is empty on every claim in ryan@ryan.com.
rca_of_issue: Original bug: claim/[id].tsx previously rendered the BROKEN ITEM value as `{claim.inside_item_name}{claim.inside_item_model && (' · Model #: ' + claim.inside_item_model)}` (two adjacent JSX expressions), so when inside_item_model was truthy the row passed TWO children to DetailRow. DetailRow's `typeof children === 'string'` check then went false and React Native rendered the raw strings outside a <Text>, throwing the 'Text strings must be rendered within a <Text>' invariant and red-screening the route. Fix collapsed both pieces into a single template-literal string so children is always a single string and DetailRow wraps it in <Text>. Verified by direct deep-link to /claim/<id>: no red screen, no pageerror, no console invariant warning.
